top.h1: Blood tests done right, reports on WhatsApp by evening.
top.p: Walk in from 6:30 am or let us come to your home. Fasting sugar, thyroid, lipid, liver, kidney, vitamins, full body packages, ECG, X-ray and ultrasound, all under one roof on Dum Dum Road.

photo.alt: A lab technician in cap, mask and gloves holds a rack of blood sample tubes in the laboratory

top.p2: Book by 9 pm the night before. Dum Dum, Nagerbazar, Lake Town, Baguiati and Airport area.

tests.h2: The tests people ask for most, with the price.
tests.p: Over 400 tests are on the full list at the counter. These are the ones a family doctor writes most often. Prices include the report on WhatsApp and a printed copy.
tests.p2: Haemoglobin, white cells, platelets. For fever, weakness, dengue follow-up.
tests.p3: Both readings. Come fasting, then return two hours after breakfast.
tests.p4: Three-month sugar average. No fasting needed.
tests.p5: Tiredness, weight change, hair fall, irregular periods.
tests.p6: Cholesterol, triglycerides, HDL, LDL. 10 to 12 hours fasting.
tests.p7: Bilirubin, SGOT, SGPT, proteins. For jaundice, fatty liver follow-up.
tests.p8: Urea, creatinine, uric acid, electrolytes. For pressure and sugar patients.
tests.p9: Both together. Bone pain, tingling, tiredness.
tests.p10: Infection, protein, sugar. Bring the first morning sample if you can.
tests.p11: Season test for fever with body ache. Platelet count included.
tests.p12: For fever lasting more than five days.
tests.p13: Blood group, CBC, sugar, thyroid, HIV, HBsAg, VDRL, urine, as the obstetrician asks.
tests.tests-note: Prices are per test. Bring the doctor's prescription if you have one; tests can also be done without a prescription. The pathologist signs every report before it goes out.

packages.h2: One morning, one needle, the whole picture.
packages.p: Packages cost less than the tests added up. Come fasting between 6:30 and 9 am. A home visit for a package is free.
packages.for: Under 40, no known illness, yearly check
packages.for2: 40 and above, or sugar and pressure in the family

items.li: Report review call from the pathologist
Free home collection, two visits if needed

home.h2: We come to you. Here is how it works.
home.h3: Where we go, and what it costs
home.p: One collector covers one zone each morning, so slots are limited to about 25 homes a day. Book early in festival season and when dengue is going around.

photo.alt: A gloved collector draws a blood sample from a patient's arm

items.p: WhatsApp a photo of the doctor's slip, or just the test names, with your address and a phone number. Book by 9 pm for the next morning.
You get a one-hour window between 6 and 11 am, the collector's name and the exact amount to pay. No surprises at the door.
The collector carries a sealed kit, gloves and a cold box. The whole thing takes ten minutes. Pay by cash or UPI then or after the report.
Routine reports reach you on WhatsApp by 7 pm the same day as a PDF. A printed copy waits at the counter if you want it.

items.span: Dum Dum, Nagerbazar, Motijheel, Lake Town, when the bill is ₹999 or more
Baguiati, Kestopur, Airport, Belgharia, Dum Dum Cantonment
Any full body package, any listed area

prepare.h2: Fasting rules and other things worth knowing.
prepare.p: Half the repeat visits we see are because of a cup of tea. Read this the night before.
prepare.p2: Reports go as a PDF to the WhatsApp number you give at the counter. If a value is far outside the normal range, the pathologist calls you the same day and suggests you see your doctor. We do not give treatment advice on the phone.

items.p: Finish dinner by 9 pm and come between 6:30 and 9 am. Plain water is fine, as much as you like. No tea, coffee, biscuits, chewing gum or paan. Fasting is needed for fasting sugar, lipid profile and some packages, not for CBC, thyroid or vitamins.

Take your pressure and thyroid tablets as usual with water. For sugar tablets or insulin, ask your doctor; most say take them after the fasting sample. Carry the medicine strip so we can note the name.
Eat your normal breakfast right after the fasting sample, note the time, and come back exactly two hours later. Do not skip or shrink the meal; the test is meant to see a normal day.

Collect the first urine of the morning in the sterile cup we give you (or buy one from any chemist for ₹10). Mid-stream, not the first few drops. Bring it within two hours. Women should avoid the test during periods unless the doctor says otherwise.
Six hours empty stomach, and drink four to five glasses of water one hour before so the bladder is full. Do not pass urine until the scan is done. For a pelvic scan the full bladder matters most.
Nothing special. Avoid heavy exercise, tea and smoking for one hour before. Wear a shirt or kurta that opens at the front. The test takes five minutes and the report is ready in fifteen.

imaging.h2: Three rooms on the first floor, no appointment for ECG and X-ray.

photo.alt: An ECG trace printed on graph paper

items.p: 12-lead, read by a physician. Walk in any time during lab hours.

photo.alt: A technician in a white coat works at the lab's automated analyser

items.p: Chest, spine, knee, hand, sinus. Film on a CD or sent as an image; radiologist report by evening.

photo.alt: A doctor listens to an elderly patient's chest with a stethoscope

items.p: Whole abdomen, pelvis, pregnancy, thyroid, KUB. Done by a visiting radiologist, Mon, Wed, Fri and Sat mornings. Book a slot.

photo.alt: A technician in protective cap and mask holds a rack of labelled blood samples

pathologist.h2: A pathologist reads every report before it leaves the lab.
pathologist.p: Dr. Sumana Ghosh, MD (Pathology), has run the lab since it opened in 2014. She checks every report personally and signs it. Abnormal smears are looked at under the microscope, not just by the machine.
pathologist.p2: The lab runs a fully automated haematology and biochemistry analyser, calibrated every morning before the first sample. Controls are run twice a day and the records are kept in a register you can ask to see. Samples go into the machine within two hours of collection.
pathologist.sig: Dr. Sumana GhoshMD (Pathology), West Bengal Medical Council registered

items.p: "My mother is 78 and cannot climb stairs. The boy came at 7, was gentle, and the report was on my phone before I left office. We do all her tests this way now."
"My thyroid value was very high and the doctor from the lab herself called to say I should see my physician soon. Nobody has done that for me before."

book.p: A photo of the doctor's slip, your address and a time that suits you. We reply with the slot and the exact amount.
